FAQ
What is EDGE Mile?
EDGE Mile is a Axis Bank loyalty currency specially defined for ATLAS credit cardholder. Each EDGE Mile worth of ₹1/-
Is EDGE Mile & EDGE Point same?
No. EDGE Mile is a loyalty currency for ATLAS credit card whereas EDGE Point is a loyalty currency for Axis Bank’s other credit cards
Where can I see the EDGE Miles?
ATLAS credit cardholder can visit EDGE Miles Section of the Axis Bank Mobile App for viewing accrued EDGE Miles
What is a tier?
Benefits on ATLAS credit card are associated with tiers. Currently, there are 3 tiers for ATLAS credit cardholder i.e. silver tier (base tier), gold tier & platinum tier (top
tier)
Where can I find my tier details?
Visit tier dashboard in the Axis Bank Mobile App
How can I upgrade my membership tier?
You can upgrade your card tier by achieving key spend Milestones at ₹7.5 lakh and ₹15 lakh. Each new tier brings in additional benefits.
Can I upgrade my tier by paying some additional fee?
No. Tier upgrade happens when ATLAS credit cardholder achieves spend milestone
How to redeem Edge Miles?
Cardholders can redeem EDGE Miles for booking flights, hotels & experiences by-
Logging into Axis Bank Mobile app & clicking on “Book Now” in EDGE Miles dashboard
Logging into https://traveledge.axisbank.co.in/
EDGE Miles can also be transferred into partner Miles under Axis Bank's Miles transfer program (where 1 EDGE Mile = 2 partner mile). Cardholders can convert EDGE Miles by –
Logging into Axis Bank Mobile app & clicking on “Book Now” in EDGE Miles dashboard
Logging into https://traveledge.axisbank.co.in/

Just like a magnetic stripe card, the CHIP and PIN enabled credit card too can be used at the merchant’s payment terminals directly. Instead of swiping the card, merchants need to ‘Dip’ your card into a CHIP reader slot.
Paying through CHIP and PIN enabled Credit Card is a 3-step process:
Dip/Swipe your card
Enter your ATM PIN
Sign on charge slip

Axis Bank Corporate Card comes with two liability options
Corporate liability: Corporate liability corporate cards are an effective way of managing travel policies and negotiating preferential terms with key suppliers. Individual Liability: Individual liability cards based on the same lines as the personal credit cards are an effective way for the employees to keep their personal and official expenses separate while at the same time simplifying the reimbursement process. Frequently Asked Questions
1. What is a Travel Credit Card?
A Travel Credit Card rewards spending with flight-related benefits, insurance coverage, and airport privileges. It is ideal for frequent flyers who travel multiple times each year. These cards are widely used across India and overseas.
2. How can you earn travel rewards or points with a Travel Credit Card?
You earn rewards by spending on flights, hotels, dining, and international purchases. Many cards offer higher reward rates for travel-related transactions. These points can later be used to reduce travel costs.
3. Are there any annual fees or hidden charges on the Travel Credit Card?
Most travel cards charge an annual fee, usually between ₹5,000 and ₹12,000. Additional costs may include foreign exchange charges and cash withdrawal fees. Many fees can be waived with sufficient annual spending.
4. What should you do if you lose your Travel Credit Card while travelling?
Immediately contact the card issuer to block the card. Most banks provide emergency assistance and replacement cards overseas. Using mobile banking apps helps manage this quickly.
5. How long do travel rewards or points last before they expire?
Reward validity depends on the issuer and card type. Typically, points remain valid for two to three years. Some premium cards offer non-expiring rewards, subject to account activity.
6. What is a Priority Pass and how does it help travellers?
A Priority Pass gives cardholders access to airport lounges across the world, regardless of the airline or class of travel. It allows travellers to relax, eat, and work comfortably before flights. Many premium Travel Credit Cards include complimentary lounge entries through this membership.
7. What does an air mile mean on a Travel Credit Card?
An air mile is a reward currency linked to airline loyalty programmes. Cardholders earn miles on eligible spending, which can later be used for flight tickets or upgrades. The value of miles depends on the airline and route chosen.
8. How can you earn reward points using a Travel Credit Card?
You earn reward points by spending on flights, hotels, dining, and international transactions. Travel-related spends usually attract higher reward rates. These points accumulate in your card account and can be used for future travel benefits.
9. How many lounge visits are usually allowed on Travel Credit Cards?
The number of lounge visits depends on the card variant and issuer. Some cards offer limited free visits per year, while premium cards provide unlimited access. International and domestic lounge limits may differ.
10. How do you redeem reward points for travel?
The points and redeem feature can be used for flight bookings, hotel stays, or travel vouchers. Redemption is usually done through airline partners or the bank’s travel portal. Using points early helps maximise value before they expire.
